candidate_kind: source-built cumulative; continues C-H2-87, drops nothing
behavioral_change: ONE: Halo 4's camera core retires on a stale camera heartbeat - armed, no owned camera frame (enginePitchSerial unchanged) for 2.5 s, not the pause screen -> armed cleared and teardown requested; the next worker tick removes the core, the title is re-detected, the runtime mode falls to unsupported and the menu/theatre presentation returns. This is the rule every other title already lives by ('once its heartbeat is absent for 500 ms, disarm per-eye rendering and release the retained scene target').
why: User: after exiting a Halo 4 level the screen stayed head-locked instead of returning to the 3D theatre and the stick went sideways in the menu. The 2026-09-01 07:58 Steam log shows the cause: the level ended ~07:59:06 (pairs 0, 'no owned Halo 4 frame in the last 250 ms' at 07:59:08.6), the title was re-detected at 07:59:09.4, the mode went gameplay->loading->gameplay in 7 ms because the still-ARMED core republished Gameplay every tick, and it stayed armed for two minutes ('camera=not seen', 0 pairs) until the module unloaded. The accepted 3CX image tore down within ~1 s at the same moment (old log: stereo OFF -> gate re-armed -> core removed -> re-detected -> unsupported). Halo 4's level-load gate never closes on its own once open, so teardown depended on the core disarming at level end; on the source build it no longer did. The heartbeat rule restores the behaviour regardless of which upstream signal changed.
safety: Exempts pause presentation; ignores the window before the first heartbeat of a generation; a hitch shorter than 2.5 s is untouched; a longer one re-earns the install through the existing level-load gate exactly as consecutive levels already do. Cinematics keep the heartbeat (the camera setup hook runs every owned frame).
log_line: 'Halo 4 camera core: no camera heartbeat for N ms while armed (the level closed) - retiring so presentation returns to the menu screen' followed by the existing 'Halo 4 camera core removed' and 'Runtime mode: ... -> unsupported'.
